prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map lays out a salon scene viewed from above and behind a seated woman (~0.5–1.2 m away, facing down and right away from the camera wearer toward a red tablet in her lap), with the camera wearer's own arms extending into the foreground (~0.15–0.5 m) holding a hairdryer on the left and a round brush below/center, while an empty salon chair (~1.8–2.2 m ahead) and tiled floor (~1.5–2.5 m below) recede into the dark background. The woman's head (~0.5–0.6 m), the hairdryer, and the round brush are all within the camera wearer's immediate arm's reach (and the tablet is ~0.3 m from her torso within her own grasp), while the wearer's lower body is out of view and the wearer's left arm/hairdryer partially occlude the woman's head and background furniture. Across the 5 frames, the left arm and hairdryer drop downward and further away in frame 3 (~0.5–0.7 m) before approaching very close to the lens in frame 4 (~0.1–0.2 m, bright white) and retreating slightly in frame 5 (~0.2–0.3 m) as the round brush pulls a hair strand downward and left. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the vertical layering between the wearer's elevated arms, the woman's head directly below them, her lower legs (~1.0–1.4 m), and the floor. However, the map looks unreliable in frame 3 where relative contrast flattens so the lowered left arm appears nearly as dark as the background (~1.0 m), and in frames 4–5 where the hairdryer's depth bleeds smoothly into the woman's hair and shoulder without a sharp boundary.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map outlines the foreground camera wearer's arms (0.15–0.5 m, left and bottom-center) interacting with the seated woman (0.5–1.4 m, center-right, facing right and angled down toward her lap away from the camera wearer) and an empty background chair (~2 m ahead at top-center in frames 1 and 4). The woman's head and hair are within the camera wearer's reach (~0.5 m) and her held tablet is within her own reach (~0.3 m from her chest), while the wearer's torso is out of view and the foreground arms/tools occlude parts of the woman's hair and upper body. Across the 5 frames, as the wearer's left arm and hairdryer lower in frame 3 and rise back over the head in frames 4–5, the masks track the shifting silhouette of the upper-left arm and the woman's seated body. While the map provides crisp pixel boundaries separating the overlapping foreground limbs from the dark salon floor that can blend together in RGB, its class labels and instance boundaries are highly unreliable. It mislabels the round hairbrush as a 'sandwich' (frame 1) or 'cell phone' (frame 5) and the red tablet as a 'toothbrush' (frames 1–2), fails to segment the hairdryer as a separate object from the 'person' masks, and fragments and merges the wearer's arms and the seated woman into inconsistent multi-person masks across all 5 frames.
descriptions.pose: The pose map isolates the 2D body (yellow) and hand (magenta) skeleton of the seated woman (~0.5–1.4 m below and in front of the camera wearer), showing her torso angled to the right, her head keypoints clustered on the left (~0.5–0.6 m away) facing downward toward her lap rather than toward the camera wearer, and her bent legs extending to the bottom-right (~1.0–1.4 m). Her left and right wrists converge ~0.3–0.4 m in front of her torso within her own arm's reach to hold the tablet, while her head sits within the camera wearer's reach even though the wearer's own arms and tools (~0.15–0.5 m) are completely unrepresented. Across the 5 frames, her skeletal posture remains nearly stationary—showing only slight shifts in her right arm and leg joints as the camera viewpoint tilts slightly—confirming that she neither turns nor approaches while the camera wearer moves above her. Unlike the RGB image where black clothing and overhead foreshortening obscure limb articulation, the skeleton clearly reveals the positions of her occluded shoulders, elbows, hips, and knees under her dark attire and behind the wearer's reaching right arm. However, the map is unreliable in omitting the camera wearer's foreground hands and arms entirely, collapsing the woman's top-down facial keypoints into an indistinct cluster on the left side of her head, and merging her right hand's magenta keypoints onto her left hand rather than tracking her right arm's wrist cleanly.
